unchanged\\u0022\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022\\u0022A project created by h9k project add records permission skipping enabled on its ProjectRegistered event, and a run dispatched on that project launches with --dangerously-skip-permissions with no h9k project set step in between\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022The field\\u0027s default ON THE EVENT RECORD is false and h9k project add explicitly passes true - this direction is load-bearing: a parameter defaulting to true would make every pre-change stream deserialize and replay as true, silently flipping every existing project, the exact outcome ruled against; ProjectRegistered.HomeDirectory is the precedent and its doc comment states the same reasoning\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022A test replays a project stream written before existing setting\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022h9k project set --skip-permissions keeps working in both directions and still overrides the registration value\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022docs/operations.md no longer presents the h9k project set --skip-permissions step as required for a new project (the example near line 482)\\u0022\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022## Background\\n\\nFrom the Windows field report (2026-08-31), item 2\\u0027s root, triaged 2026-09-01: SkipPermissions on the project aggregate is a plain bool with no initializer, ProjectRegistered does not carry the value, and h9k project add has no flag for it - so every newly registered project starts with permission prompts live, and per the field report that kills every headless run (the worktree\\u0027s .git file points at the bare clone outside the session\\u0027s allowed directory, so every git call needs an approval no headless session can give). The Windows deployment registered a project the normal way and every run died, diagnosable only from the transcript. This is a first-run experience defect, not a misconfiguration.\\n\\nRuling (Brian, 2026-09-01): a new project registers with permission skipping ON, applying to headless and interactive alike - he explicitly does not want the distinction - and this must not reach back and change any project that already exists.\\n\\nExplicitly out of scope, ruled noise or parked - do not let these creep back in during grooming or review: no --skip-permissions flag on project add, no warning when someone sets it false, no permission-denial classifier for the \\u0022Agent produced no commits\\u0022 reason (parked, not killed - that reason remains the catch-all for silent deaths, but this report is no longer its evidence), no h9k doctor or dispatch preflight, no composition of the launched session\\u0027s settings file.\\n\\n## Sequencing\\n\\nThis is the six-file shared-append-point shape AGENTS.md describes for a project setting (ProjectRegistered, ProjectDecider, ProjectAggregate, ProjectDetails, the CLI command, the registration). Never assign it in parallel with another task adding a project setting.\\n\\nPriority ruling (Brian, 2026-09-01): published and deliberately UNASSIGNED - gap-filler work, done when more important work leaves a gap. Published-unassigned is the platform\\u0027s low-priority posture (nothing dispatches an unassigned task); the same posture 28e400d9 and f260ebf6 worktree is removed, and the run completes, exactly as the watched path does\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022The pull request is recorded on the RUN side so an existing sweep finds it - do not add a fourth The orphan sweep exists for precisely this shape (Decisions Log #72: a Failed or Killed run whose pull request does not stop existing because nothing is watching it), and resolve --pr is Failed-only so the run state already qualifies; the only missing piece is that nothing ever writes the number and URL onto RunDetails\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022LOAD-BEARING TRAP: do not do this by appending PullRequestOpened. RunDetails.Apply(PullRequestOpened) sets State to AwaitingReview, which would move a Failed run into the WATCHED sweep instead of the orphan one - the watched path dispatches follow-up runs onto the branch, and InspectOrphanAsync\\u0027s own doc comment says inventing a follow-up onto a dead run\\u0027s branch is not that sweep\\u0027s job. The run must stay Failed, which points at a new run-stream event recording the pull request without changing state; the exact shape is the implementing session\\u0027s call\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022The closeout side effects fire exactly once: ReconstructAndCompleteAsync already guards double-completion (a second completion would double the merge comment, the handoff, and the dependents-unblock), and whatever path this takes must not reopen that hole\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022A resolve with no --pr is unchanged in every respect\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022AttentionComposer\\u0027s Failed/Killed arm stops rendering \\u0027nothing is watching this pull request any more\\u0027 for a task whose pull request is now watched, so the pane does not contradict the behaviour\\u0022\u0022,\u0022\\u0022Tests cover the whole path (resolve --pr on a failed run, the pull request then merges, closeout completes) plus the negative (a resolve without --pr never enters the sweep)\\u0022\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022## Background\\n\\nWindows field report item 6\\u0027s bug half, ruled 2026-09-01 (the adopt-an-existing-PR FEATURE stays parked under Brian\\u0027s 2026-08-31 ruling, reconfirmed today: item 9 removes the rename-recovery reason for hand-opened pull requests and stacked-PR slice 1 removes the stacking reason, leaving roughly the one-time migration case).\\n\\nThe bug exists independently of any feature: h9k task resolve --pr is a shipped, documented recovery lever whose recorded pull request is watched by nothing. TaskDetails.Apply(TaskResolved) writes the URL onto the task projection only; RunDetails.PullRequestNumber is set solely by PullRequestOpened, PullRequestUpdated, and RunRecordReconstructed, so the orphan sweep (which filters on it) never matches, and the missing-run sweep skips too because the failed run does have a RunDetails row. It falls exactly between the two sweeps, and the board row sits needs-you forever.
